title: Enteral Nutrition in Pediatric Patients Undergoing Hematopoietic SCT Promotes the Recovery of Gut Microbiome Homeostasis
population: Twenty pediatric patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation at Sant’Orsola-Malpighi Hospital-University of Bologna, Italy; 10 received enteral nutrition and 10 received parenteral nutrition after transplantation.
intervention: Enteral nutrition for more than 7 days post-HSCT (n=10).
comparator: Total parenteral nutrition, or enteral feeding for less than 7 days post-HSCT, classified in the parenteral-nutrition group (n=10).
outcomes: Gut microbiome alpha diversity (observed ASVs and Faith’s Phylogenetic Diversity)
Gut microbiome beta diversity and community structure (weighted and unweighted UniFrac; PCoA)
Taxonomic relative abundance at phylum, family, and genus levels
Fecal short-chain fatty acid concentrations (total SCFAs, acetate, propionate, butyrate)
Acute graft-versus-host disease occurrence and severity
Mucositis, engraftment, and outcome at day +100
funding: This work was supported by the Italian Ministero della Salute (Bando Ricerca Finalizzata 2013, Giovani Ricercatori section, code GR-2013-02357136 to R.M.).
conflicts_of_interest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
